extracted.intended_audience: TeX/LaTeX (and plain TeX/ConTeXt) users writing graphics with pgf/TikZ — authors of documents that include programmatic graphics
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and rules for producing and managing graphics with the pgf/TikZ system: coordinate/canvas transforms, patterns, images, masking, and externalizing (extracting) graphics into separate files. Covers command semantics, pitfalls, and recommended workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: \ifpgfslopedattime
rubrics_metrics.description: Decides whether the “at time” transformation commands also rotate coordinates or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When true, line-at-time and curve-at-time transformations may apply an additional rotation to align with the curve/line slope. This affects text orientation inserted after such transforms; interacts with \ifpgfallowupsidedowattime and \ifpgfresetnontranslationsattime settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: \ifpgfallowupsidedowattime
rubrics_metrics.description: Decides whether the “at time” transformation commands should allow the rotation be down in such a way that “upside-down text” can result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If false, pgf will ensure text is never upside-down; if true, rotated text may be inverted depending on slope decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: \ifpgfresetnontranslationsattime
rubrics_metrics.description: Decides whether the “at time” transformation commands should reset the non-translations between shifting and rotating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If true, pgf calls \pgftransformresetnontranslations between shifting and rotating; impacts whether rotation/scale from the current CTM affect the placement/orientation when using 'at time' transforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute coordinate transformation commands are potentially dangerous
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands that set the coordinate transformation matrix “absolutely” (rather than concatenating) can produce unexpected effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use absolute-transform commands only if you really know what you're doing; they override prior transformations and may break assumptions elsewhere in a scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgftransformreset
rubrics_metrics.description: Resets the coordinate transformation matrix to the identity matrix. Once issued, no coordinate transformations are applied until the end of the scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to cancel all transforms; example shows resetting after a scale+rotate so subsequent drawing uses plain coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgftransformresetnontranslations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets the a,b,c,d parts of the coordinate transformation matrix to 1,0,0,1 respectively, leaving the shift (translation) unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Undo rotation/scaling/slanting but keep origin shift. Mostly useful immediately before \pgftext to ensure text is not scaled or rotated; example contrasts rotated vs shifted-only text.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgftransforminvert
rubrics_metrics.description: Replaces the current coordinate transformation matrix by its exact inverse (the transform that undoes the original transformation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produces an error if the matrix determinant is too small (near-singular). Example: inverts 'scale by 2 then shift right by 1cm' into 'shift left by 1cm then scale by 1/2'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving and restoring coordinate transforms (\pgfgettransform / \pgfsettransform)
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfgettransform{\macro} defines \macro to a representation of the current CTM; \pgfsettransform{\macro} reinstalls a previously saved transform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to capture a CTM and reapply it later; saved macro is local and can be used to restore complex transform states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canvas vs coordinate transformations — key distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Canvas transformations (managed by backend) differ from coordinate transformations: they apply to everything (images, text, line thickness), are local to {pgfscope} (not TEX group), cannot be reset, and pgf does not track them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because canvas transforms are applied after the graphic is finished and handled by the driver, pgf cannot correctly save coordinates of shapes/nodes when canvas transforms are used. Be cautious when combining canvas transforms with pgf operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgflowlevelsynccm
rubrics_metrics.description: Concatenates the canvas transformation matrix with the current coordinate transformation matrix, then resets the coordinate transformation matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectively synchronizes CTM and canvas TM: transformations previously applied by coordinate transforms become canvas transforms. Useful when you want the backend to perform the transform (affects everything including line widths). Example shows scale then a short draw; coordinate CTM reset afterward.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgflowlevel / \pgflowlevelobj / \beginpgflowlevelscope
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands/environments to concatenate an arbitrary coordinate transformation with the canvas transform (via \pgflowlevel) for a scoped piece of code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows you to apply a coordinate transform at canvas level (so it affects everything) for just the enclosed drawing; several variants exist including object-wrapping and environment forms for plain TeX/ConTeXt compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patterns: inherently colored vs form-only patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two kinds of tiling patterns: inherently colored patterns (tile has its own color) and form-only patterns (tile is like a rubber stamp; color provided on use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form-only patterns accept a color parameter when set; inherently colored patterns ignore the color parameter and must set color via pgf color commands. Once declared, a pattern cannot be changed (size, line width, etc.). Also, pattern phase/origin may differ across backends (pdf/PostScript vs SVG), so expect differences in alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfdeclarepatternformonly requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaration form: \pgfdeclarepatternformonly{name}{lower left}{upper right}{tile size}{code}. The code should be pgf code that can be protocolled and should not contain any color code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: lower-left/upper-right define a bounding box that must encompass the tile; tile size sets the tile rectangle with origin at lower-left. Bounding box may be smaller or larger than tile size causing clipping or bleed. For form-only patterns avoid color setting inside the code; color supplied later via \pgfsetfillpattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfdeclarepatterninherentlycolored requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaration for an inherently colored pattern: same parameters as form-only but the pattern contains its own colors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To set the tile's color use pgf's color commands (e.g., \pgfsetfillcolor), not \color, since pattern code is protocolled differently. The color parameter passed to \pgfsetfillpattern is ignored for inherently colored patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsetfillpattern behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfsetfillpattern{name}{color} specifies that fills should use the named pattern with the given color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For form-only patterns the color argument is used to tint the stamp; for inherently colored patterns the color argument is ignored. Once a pattern is declared its geometry/line widths cannot be changed at use time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer \includegraphics over pgfbaseimage when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: LATEX's \includegraphics (graphicx) is generally better designed than pgfbaseimage; use it unless you need pgf-specific features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pgfbaseimage only if your format lacks a standard include mechanism (plain TeX) or you need features pgf offers, notably masking. For most workflows, \includegraphics is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-phase image workflow (declare then use) vs immediate use
rubrics_metrics.description: pgf suggests declaring images with \pgfdeclareimage{name}{filename} and later inserting them with \pgfuseimage{name}; \pgfimage declares and immediately uses the image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaring first ensures the image data is included only once in the output (reduces file size if the image is reused). Use \pgfimage when you want a quick declare+use and don't need reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for \pgfdeclareimage
rubrics_metrics.description: Supported options include height, width (each preserves aspect ratio if the other omitted), page (select page from multipage document), interpolate (true/false for smoothing when zoomed), and mask (a previously declared mask name).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: page option tries an alternate filename 'name.pageN.ext' before falling back to page extraction in pdftex; interpolate defaults to false; mask works only for pdf backend and pixel-format images (.jpg/.png).

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfaliasimage (image aliasing)
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfaliasimage{new}{existing} clones an image name so the new name can be used wherever the existing image is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for creating alternate-named variants (e.g., for alternate extensions or accessing the last inserted image pgflastimage). Example: aliasing color-mixin variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfuseimage / \pgfimage fallback and \pgfalternateextension
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfuseimage inserts a previously declared image; if \pgfalternateextension expands to a nonempty alternate extension string, pgf first tries image.name.alternateext and iteratively strips segments up to '!' to try fallbacks before using the original image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: xxcolor sets alternate extension to current color mixin (e.g., '!25!white'); \pgfimage declares then uses an image and stores it as pgflastimage. Using \pgfalternateextension allows automatic selection of color-mixed variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masking images (\pgfdeclaremask) requirements and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare a transparency mask with \pgfdeclaremask{name}{filename}. The mask file must be a grayscale (single channel) image same size as the actual image; white pixels correspond to transparent, black to solid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Masking works only for images in pixel formats (.jpg, .png), not for .pdf images. The mask and image must match dimensions. Option 'matte={color components}' sets the preblend matte color of the masked image (default {1 1 1} white); matte specified in parent's image color space. Not all viewers support masking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Externalizing graphics workflow (declare, generate, include)
rubrics_metrics.description: To externalize pictures: (1) mark each picture with \beginpgfgraphicnamed{fileprefix} ... \endpgfgraphicnamed, (2) set \pgfrealjobname{realname} and run TeX with --jobname=graphicname to produce single-file graphics, (3) rerun TeX normally to include the generated graphic files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 2 causes pgf to swallow the full document except the named graphic and produce a single-page file sized to the graphic. Use pdflatex --jobname=... to generate .pdf outputs or latex+dvips for .ps. This workflow speeds compilation and produces standalone figure files acceptable to publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming external graphics: uniqueness and filesystem safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Each graphic that will be externalized should have a unique name which becomes a filename; names should not contain funny characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an external file with that name already exists, \beginpgfgraphicnamed will include that file (via \includegraphics) and ignore the code between the begin/end. Note: inclusion ignores the code without macro expansion, so macros used inside needn't be defined when included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior when generating external graphics (\jobname equals graphic name)
rubrics_metrics.description: When \jobname equals a graphic name and \pgfrealjobname was declared, pgf collects everything between the matching \beginpgfgraphicnamed and \endpgfgraphicnamed into a box and ships out only that box as the document output, with page size equal to the box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The normal shipout is temporarily replaced to discard other output; at the end the single-page file contains precisely the graphic. This is how pdflatex --jobname=survey-f1 survey.tex produces survey-f1.pdf with just the figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including external graphics without pgf installed (pgfexternal.tex)
rubrics_metrics.description: To produce a document suitable for publishers without pgf installed, input pgfexternal.tex which redefines \beginpgfgraphicnamed to \includegraphics{#1} and gobbles to \endpgfgraphicnamed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lets you keep the original source (with tikz code commented out) but include the pre-generated graphics automatically. Note that the baseline option does not work with pictures written to external graphic files because baseline information cannot be stored in external files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern and image backend portability pitfalls
rubrics_metrics.description: Some pattern and image behaviors differ between backends: pattern phase/origin differs (pdf/PostScript define fixed origin; svg may use path's upper-left corner and is vague); masking only works for certain backends and formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect rendering differences across output formats; avoid relying on precise tile-phase alignment or pattern mutability. For portability prefer simple fills or test on target backend(s).
